item.title: COMING Saturday SEPT. 19th | Pisgah Brewing Presents: Son Volt with Shannon McNally — Thu Sep 10 — Pisgah Brewing Company Black Mountain
item.description:
Saturday, September 19, 2026 7:30 PM | Doors Open: 6:00 PM | Outdoor Stage | $36.15 adv. Event Details and Tickets
After spearheading the alt-country movement with Uncle Tupelo, Jay Farrar pursued his vision with Son Volt, who recorded three landmark albums in the ’90s before the groundbreaking artist put the band on extended hiatus and cut three solo LPs. Missing the free exchange of ideas and the surprises that inevitably occur when a group of simpatico musicians lock together, Farrar assembled a new lineup of Son Volt in 2004 and has since released nine albums. The latest album, Sound Signal Serenades, was released as a special 2026 Record Store Day limited edition LP. Jay Farrar’s work often seeks out the ghosts of America’s discordant or forgotten past, converses at length with them, and writes songs that stake a claim to a better future.

item.title: Inner Child Playshop — Sun Sep 13, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Awakening Asheville You're invited to the best play date of the year. Who's inviting you? Your inner child. And they want you to know; it's been too long since the two of you spent time together doing things that bring you joy and wonder.
Senseful Wellness is pairing up with Ayla Claypool for an afternoon that is equal parts intentional and delightfully unserious. A three-hour hang designed for the part of you that still knows how to play.
Ayla will guide everyone through a series of games using techniques from physical theatre theorist Jacques Lecoq in order to open our spacial and emotional awareness and take steps toward transformation. Exploratory and silly, serious play asks everyone the question of what does it mean to move like a kid again. To find the joy.
Vi will open and close the Playshop calling in your inner child and creating the container for them to actually show up and stay a while.

item.title: Appalachian Flooding in Fact and Fiction — Wed Sep 16, 5:30 PM
item.description:
In “Appalachian Flooding in Fact and Fiction,” Nico Zegre, Ph.D., explores how floods work, what flooding looks like in Appalachia, and why floods are changing. He will discuss how the region’s steep topography, narrow valleys, and limited flat land for development contribute to significant flood risks, as well as how flooding connects Appalachian communities through space and time. Literary scholar Jessica Cory, Ph.D., examines representations of flooding in Appalachian literature, from early works to contemporary depictions in twenty-first-century texts, including the recent anthologies Had I a Dove: Appalachian Poets on the Helene Flood, edited by Hilda Downer, and Troublesome Rising: A Thousand-Year Flood in Eastern Kentucky, edited by Melissa Helton. Through mapping literary floods across the region, Cory explores how water connects us, even in disastrous ways. This event is free and open to the public; however, registration is encouraged. item.title: Gaming Night @ Noble Cider — Tue Sep 29, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Asheville's Bored Game Geeks Roll the dice and pour a glass! 🎲🍎
Gaming Night is back at Noble Cider! Join us every other Tuesday for a night of tabletop tactics, card-shuffling chaos, and great company. Whether you’re a seasoned strategist or you still think a "meeple" is a type of small fruit, you’re welcome at our table.
### The Lowdown:
* **No Experience? No Problem:** We’re all about community. We’ll help you learn the ropes of a new game or cheer you on while you figure it out. * **The Library:** We have a solid stash of games ready to play—from quick party favorites to deeper strategy titles. * **Bring Your Favorites:** Have a game gathering dust on your shelf? **Feel Free to bring your own games too!**

item.title: Fall Tree ID — Fri Oct 2, 1:00 PM
item.description:
Fall Tree ID With Hannah Lilly and Ben Warfield Friday, October 2 | 1pm – 3pm BRN – Core | BREG – Elective Register Here!
Join this group as we talk about how to identify the trees of Western North Carolina as they start to lose their leaves. Many of our native species are identifiable even when they’re dormant, and learning this practice is a rewarding and useful skill for all naturalists. We will talk about how to use the bark, twigs, and more to be able to recognize new and familiar trees in our region. This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. Hannah Lilly is a Botanist and Ecologist interested in the connection between plants, people, and their environment. item.description:
Bonsai in a Day: Learn, Create, Take Home with Rebecca Ayres Saturday, October 3 | 9:30 am – 4:30pm Register Here!
Although it has its roots in ancient Asian traditions, the living art of bonsai now enjoys enthusiasts throughout much of the world. This class will provide the basic concepts and skills for novices to begin growing and shaping their own miniature trees. The first half of the class will cover the fundamental horticultural and aesthetic principles of bonsai. It will include such topics as tree selection, watering, pest control, pruning, wiring, and styling. In the second half of the class, each participant will receive a pot, scissors, wire, and planting medium. With guidance from the instructor, the students will create their own bonsai to take home. Materials included in registration. Rebecca Ayres is a ceramic artist and gardener. item.title: Lea and Heffernan of Wheelchair Sports Camp — Fri Oct 9, 3:00 PM
item.description:
Gaelynn Lea and Kalyn Rose Heffernan of Wheelchair Sports Camp will visit UNC Asheville for an afternoon talk and evening performance. At 3 p.m., Lea and Heffernan will discuss disability culture, access, and activism, sharing their experiences as artists and advocates working to make the arts more inclusive. At 6 p.m., Wheelchair Sports Camp will take the stage for a free performance. Lea, winner of NPR Music’s Tiny Desk Contest, is an accomplished violinist, songwriter, composer, and disability advocate who has performed around the world and composed the score for Macbeth on Broadway. Wheelchair Sports Camp, led by wheelchair-using rapper Kalyn Rose Heffernan, blends hip-hop, humor, and high-energy performance. The Denver-based band has expanded its work beyond music into performance art, museums, theater, film, and activism. Both events are free and open to the public and will take place in the Blue Ridge Room of the Highsmith Student Union.
